description: Temporary disability is a cornerstone of the public Social Security system. It is a right for all workers who fall ill and a social security benefit designed primarily to protect those who are sick, enabling them to receive medical treatment and recover or improve their condition while ensuring they have sufficient income during periods in which they are unable to work.
title: Workplace absenteeism: Why temporary disability is a right, not an expense

description: Want to break down some basics in the world of quantum research over dinner? Researchers at the Cockrell School of Engineering have you covered.
title: New light-conversion tool could help speed up quantum computing

description: For many, the year 2026 will be remembered as the one when mathematics had an identity crisis and forever changed. Frontier (cutting-edge) AI models made by OpenAI and Anthropic made stunning progress on hundreds of open problems that have baffled mathematicians for decades—and centuries in some cases.
title: AI has solved a host of big math problems—here's why this threatens the whole field of mathematics

description: There is a widespread notion among violinists: A violin "opens up" as it is played, which is to say its sound gradually improves. However, an experiment conducted by a team led by a CNRS researcher has challenged this belief in a study published in Acta Acustica. After six months, the professional soloist in charge of playing the violin judged the process complete, reporting that the instrument had become easier to play and its tone had improved. Yet, no physical or acoustic measurement confirmed that this feeling resulted from such a mechanical change in the instrument itself.
title: Do a violin's physical characteristics really improve with regular playing?

description: Darwin's finches are known for their varied beaks, which help them take advantage of different food sources in the Galápagos Islands. Much previous research has focused on seed-eating ground finches, but their relatives that search for insects in forested areas have received less attention.
title: Genetic mosaic helps explain diverse forms of Darwin's finches

description: More people around the world will receive a cancer diagnosis at some point in their lives. As this trend is expected to continue, researchers have been working to crack the code of how the widely used cancer drug Taxol (paclitaxel) is naturally produced, with the aim of making its production cheaper and more efficient in the future.
title: Recipe for one of the world's most important cancer drugs uncovered: Tobacco plants could produce the medicine

description: A quantum device with more qubits is harder to verify. Describing a general quantum state takes an exponential number of parameters, and reconstructing it in full—a procedure known as state tomography—becomes impractical as the system grows. Yet most experiments do not need the full description. They need to know a few things: Is the state close to the target? Are the qubits entangled? And does the system carry the resources needed for quantum computation?
title: Local measurements reveal global quantum properties in a constant number of experimental runs

description: Mpox remains a smoldering threat, with recent clusters in Brazil, Thailand and Austria and ongoing hot spots across multiple African countries. Other poxviruses also endanger human or animal health. A new study by the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) uncovers the inner workings of the poxvirus core: how its gene-copying machines sit parked in dormant pairs, ready to print viral instructions and release them into the host cell through dedicated export portals embedded in the core shell.
title: Electron microscopy reveals the headquarters of poxviruses

description: Most online shoppers know that ads strategically follow them across sites, a mechanism known as "ad retargeting." A new study led by Penn State researchers found that consumers find these targeted ads helpful, but explaining why they are seeing an ad can backfire by increasing concerns about being watched.
title: Consumers, oblivious of being targeted, find online ads helpful

description: A Southwest Research Institute-led study is the first to map out the distinct motion paths of the heliotail lobes across a 14-year period using data from NASA's Interstellar Boundary Explorer (IBEX) spacecraft. By identifying the paths followed by these lobes, the study provides a better understanding of how solar activity shapes the heliotail.
title: NASA spacecraft data reveal how solar system's tail shifts over 14 years

description: Medical imaging technologies have transformed how scientists and physicians visualize blood flowing through the human heart, but even the most advanced imaging techniques cannot capture every detail of fluid motion. Researchers at the University of California, Irvine, have developed a computational approach that combines fundamental physics with artificial intelligence to reconstruct a more complete and accurate picture of fluid flow from limited and imperfect measurements.
title: Physics-guided AI reconstructs fluid flow from sparse, noisy data

description: Myanmar amber (more commonly known as "burmite") is one of the most important sources of information about biodiversity during the Mesozoic Era. This amber dates back to the age of the dinosaurs and is approximately 99 million years old. Burmite preserves numerous now-extinct organisms (animals, plants, fungi, etc.) as inclusions, often in astonishing detail. This is because amber can preserve even soft tissues, which would otherwise decompose rapidly, and do so in three dimensions.
title: A nearly 100-million-year-old hairy snail pays tribute to the Prodigy's lead singer

description: In the desert, water doesn't arrive steadily. It comes in short pulses: a winter storm, a few rainy days, then months of drought. A desert plant needs two skills to live there. It has to survive the long dry spells, and it has to make full use of the brief windows when water is plentiful. A new study from Ben-Gurion University of the Negev and the Volcani Institute shows that the prickly pear cactus has an unexpected way of doing both.
title: A cactus that changes gears: How the prickly pear makes the most of desert rain

description: For more than half a century, physicists searching for a grand unified theory have followed one unspoken rule: go bigger. If you want to weave nature's fundamental forces into a single mathematical framework, the classic recipe says you need a giant "simple" symmetry group—structures like SU(5) or SO(10) that act like massive algebraic warehouses large enough to hold every force at once.
title: Overlooked symmetry group offers new geometric blueprint for the Standard Model and topologically protected vacuums

description: Researchers discovered that the biological machinery behind flower color also helps shape fragrance. By disrupting a single gene in petunias, they changed the flowers' mix of scent compounds, increasing some associated with vanilla and cloves.
title: A hidden link between a flower's color and its scent revealed

description: In South Africa, more than 2 million smallholder households make a living through agriculture. Within this small-scale farming sector, roughly 613,000 families own cattle. They farm on shared rural rangelands.
title: South Africa's small cattle farmers need help before super El Niño hits: How to set up shade, water and feed

description: A complication of diabetes is that damaged bones don't heal well, but a group of researchers is helping solve the problem with a novel mechanism to help bone regeneration.
title: Nanoparticles repair mitochondria to boost bone regeneration in diabetic rats

description: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope has painted a vibrant tapestry of the legendary supernova remnant Cassiopeia A (Cas A). Remnants like these are the clouds of gas and dust that remain following the explosion of a massive star and will eventually seed a new generation of stars and planets.
title: Webb finds evidence star's layers may have merged just hours before Cas A supernova

description: As we gear up to eventually land a human on Mars, more and more ideas are coming out about how to prepare for that. A recent one from Pioneer Labs, a research institute founded by bioengineer Erika DeBenedictis to develop biological technologies for space exploration, is now available on the arXiv preprint server, without any plans to release it in a paid journal as part of the "Open Science" policy of The Astera Institute.
title: Bacteria and nuclear power could grow ready-made homes on Mars before astronauts arrive

description: The European Space Agency's Hera mission for planetary defense surveys its target asteroids with a combination of instruments, peering beyond the limits of the human eye. The larger Didymos asteroid—dominated by its dramatic equatorial ridge—is seen here from just 28.5 km (17.7 miles) away, variously in visible light, multispectral and thermal infrared vision.
title: Hera surveys asteroids with superhuman vision

description: The artificial intelligence boom has brought with it debates about where the data centers that run the technology will be located, how big they will be and how to ensure communities benefit from them. Underlying these debates is the question of whether state and local governments should ban them outright, welcome them with open arms or choose something in between.
title: Data center policy review reveals 'chaotic' patchwork of rules across all 50 states

description: Delivering on its promise, the European Space Agency's EarthCARE satellite is already yielding new insights into the role that clouds play in regulating Earth's climate. The latest findings shed light on one of the processes that leads to the breakup of vast, bright cloud formations that help keep our planet cool—with rain emerging as a key driver.
title: Satellite observations show how rain breaks up Earth's natural sunshades

description: Roughly half of the world's population speaks more than one language. But speaking two or three languages is very different from claiming proficiency in five, 10 or more.
title: Some people claim to speak many languages. But what does it really mean to be a polyglot?

description: At the Commonwealth summit in Antigua in November 2026, Britain's King Charles expressed sorrow for Britain's role in the slave trade.
title: Reparations can work when claims are grounded in solid evidence

description: Stars used to calibrate the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) must have precisely characterized spectra so that their fluxes can be measured accurately. Yet some stars that appear single may in fact harbor unresolved companions that alter their predicted radiation. One such object, HD 158485—an A-type star in the JWST calibration program—has now been shown to be a binary system whose two stars both pulsate.
title: Stellar pulses reveal hidden binary in JWST calibration star sample

description: Pure rapeseed honey—or not quite? Single-flower honeys must contain a certain proportion of pollen from the respective plant. This is assessed by pollen analysis, which is time-consuming and requires specialist expertise. As part of a collaborative project, a research team from the Helmholtz Centre for Environmental Research (UFZ) and the German Centre for Integrative Biodiversity Research (iDiv) in Leipzig worked with several partners to develop an automated, AI-based pollen analysis method for honey testing.
title: Which pollen is found in honey? Automated analysis closely matches conventional testing

description: The discovery of 40 charred papyrus fragments at a temple in the ancient city of Thebes is changing researchers' understanding of one of ancient Egypt's most famous curse rituals. The fragments show that the ritual was probably far more widespread and commonplace than previously believed.
title: Discovery of curse ritual in trash dump surprises Egyptologist: 'It must have been widespread in ancient Egypt'

description: Deep inside the Chernobyl exclusion zone, where radiation levels have remained unsafe for people for the past 40 years, black molds climb the walls of the damaged former nuclear plant in Ukraine. They're entirely undeterred by the radiation—in fact, some fungi even grow toward it.
title: A fungus that can survive in Chernobyl could help create materials that trap and break down nerve agents and pesticides

description: The super El Niño developing in the Pacific is expected to strengthen toward the end of 2026 and persist into early 2027. It's set to intensify dangerous heat and cause severe drought across parts of Africa. This is likely to mean more heat-related illness and deaths, worsening water shortages and greater disruption to electricity, food supplies and essential services.
title: Super El Niño will add to Africa's heat crisis—how governments can protect people before it peaks

description: As the month of Scorpio rolls over, Flinders University researchers have been taking a close look at a rare prehistoric scorpion.
title: 310 million-year-old fossil reveals scorpion that looked much like modern relatives

description: Croatia and Costa Rica are the countries with the highest sustainable development in the world, as revealed by a new Sustainable Development Index (SDI) developed by researchers at ICTA-UAB.
title: Croatia and Costa Rica lead countries in sustainable development—while Norway ranks near bottom

description: The last of the Neanderthals died out in Europe around the same time that our own species, Homo sapiens, was spreading across the continent. Were these two events connected, or was it just a coincidence?
title: New study reveals how modern humans may have driven Neanderthals to extinction

description: An international team of astronomers led by Wouter Vlemmings and Miora Andriantsaralaza, both from Chalmers, have imaged a nearby star in unprecedented detail, using the telescope ALMA in Chile.
title: Star's record eruption shows how key elements can spread through space

description: Turning genes on and off requires transcription factors—proteins that bind specific stretches of DNA and help control gene activity. But DNA is not laid out bare inside the nucleus. It is wrapped around proteins and folded into chromatin, which can make some regions easier to reach than others.
title: How DNA's surroundings shape gene regulation

description: Why do some people remain single while others find romantic partners? And does being single necessarily mean being less happy?
title: Why are some people single—and what makes them happy? New research offers answers

description: From space, the Amazon rainforest looks like an unbroken expanse of green. But a new study conducted by researchers from the School of Biological Sciences at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), together with international collaborators, reveals seasonal leaf changes hidden within this seemingly constant canopy. Largely undetected by conventional satellite observations, these changes have significant implications for estimating the rainforest's carbon uptake.
title: Hidden leaf dynamics could improve Amazon rainforest carbon uptake estimates

description: A year after scientists at the Smithsonian Tropical Research Institute (STRI) in Panama reported the first recorded failure of the Gulf of Panama's seasonal upwelling, a follow-up study now documents how that failure moved through the system, from wind to plankton to fish to exports, using records that fishing companies rarely share.
title: When the upwelling failed, Panama's fish oil trade collapsed within months

description: Like humans, the ocean breathes. And when it does, a new study shows that far more is happening than researchers have previously assumed. "We can see that the ocean's chemical breathing is far more diverse and dynamic than we previously thought," says Mehrshad Foroughan, a postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Biology who is the first author of the new study.
title: Baltic Sea measurements reveal more complex ocean-atmosphere exchanges than previously assumed

description: A research team has identified the essential conditions required for "green budgeting"—a core fiscal policy for tackling climate change—to succeed. The team was led by professor Rosa Minhyo Cho (with doctoral candidate Minjung Kim as first author) from the Graduate School of Governance at Sungkyunkwan University (SKKU).
title: Key to successful 'green budgeting' uncovered

description: For a mollusk to build its shell, it uses brittle chalk—crystalline calcite—which must take in other materials to make the chalk stronger. That process of incorporation has long been a mystery—one that Professor Lara Estroff has been working on for her entire career.
title: How shells are made: New insights elucidate crystals' uptake of 'disruptors'

description: New York University researchers have built a way to observe bacteria as they typically live: in confinement. The research, published in the journal Small, introduces microscopic traps that mimic the tiny crevices where bacteria actually live—for instance, in soil or in our mouths.
title: Microscopic chambers reveal how bacteria navigate tight spots

description: ATRX is an ATP-dependent chromatin remodeler that helps maintain genome stability. Mutations in ATRX cause ATR-X syndrome and are found in several types of cancer. ATRX is best known for working with the histone chaperone DAXX to deposit the histone variant H3.3 in heterochromatin, where it helps maintain gene silencing and chromatin integrity. However, how ATRX regulates its own ATPase activity, uses ATP to remodel nucleosomes and functions in accessible chromatin remains unclear.
title: Study reveals dual roles for ATRX in nucleosome remodeling and histone chaperoning

description: The Hall effect, a physical phenomenon in which a current arises perpendicular to a voltage applied across a material, has been of particular interest to physicists since it was discovered more than a century ago. Over time, physicists have broadened their understanding of the Hall effect, describing quantum and anomalous versions that appear under nonclassical conditions. Recently, Rice University's Qimiao Si published a paper in Physical Review Letters describing a new variant called the fully nonequilibrium response that once again expands how physicists understand the Hall effect.
title: No magnets needed: Extreme voltage drives completely new kind of Hall effect

description: Medical experts suspect that high levels of air pollution exacerbate the symptoms of hay fever patients. Researchers at the Max Planck Institute for Chemistry in Mainz (MPIC) have now solved a chemical puzzle: When pollen allergens encounter peroxynitrite, the allergens undergo surprisingly systematic changes. New chemical groups are attached at specific exposed sites on the protein. In addition, it "glues" or links the allergens together. The findings are published in the journal Free Radical Research.
title: Oxidative stress alters and 'clogs' grass pollen allergens, study finds

description: A new high-resolution modeling tool is offering one of the clearest pictures yet of how climate change could affect a vital part of the marine food chain in Northwest European seas. The machine learning model developed by researchers at the University of Strathclyde predicts how zooplankton—tiny drifting animals that underpin marine ecosystems—could respond to changing ocean conditions over the coming decades.
title: New modeling tool sheds light on how climate change could reshape marine ecosystems

description: Femtosecond lasers produce pulses lasting only quadrillionths of a second. Their speed makes them useful for imaging rapid processes, sampling high-frequency signals and measuring distance or time with high precision. For these applications, a laser must provide not only short pulses and a broad spectrum but also stable output. Fluctuations in pulse intensity or timing can reduce image quality and measurement accuracy.
title: New fiber laser combines ultrashort pulses with broad spectrum and stable output

description: A new study reveals a previously unknown bacterial immune mechanism in which the signaling molecule 2′,3′-cGAMP triggers the splitting of the bacterial membrane into two distinct bilayers, leading to the death of infected cells and preventing further phage propagation.
title: Bacteria split their membranes to kill infected cells and block viral spread, study shows

description: The increasing use of large health care databases has exposed a fundamental statistical weakness: the assumption that bigger data sets automatically produce more reliable findings. A review of a large health care database associated with vaccination and cancer in the International Journal of Medical Engineering and Informatics shows that in practice, standard statistical methods can generate misleading levels of significance, masking underlying flaws in the data.
title: Significance and stats: Massive sample sizes do not guarantee reliable findings, study suggests

description: Countries have agreed on new measures to speed up efforts aimed at preventing the harmful effects of chemical products on health and the environment, the U.N. said.
title: Countries agree on new ways to achieve safe chemical use

description: Much of our genome contains mobile pieces or "transposable elements": pieces of DNA that spread and accumulated over millions of years, some originating from ancient viruses. Although many are no longer mobile, their sequences can influence when nearby genes switch on or off.
title: Proteins with ancient viral roots guard genetic switches left by mobile DNA

description: Researchers have reconstructed a surge–detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan, revealing how a period of rapid glacier acceleration culminated in two successive large-scale ice-detachment events.
title: Study reveals surge-detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in Pamir Mountains

description: Women are frequently sexualized in the media, which leads to their widespread objectification in society and worsens their mental health on a large scale.
title: How self-perception influences the way women view sexualized images

description: Understanding earthquake mechanisms and mitigating earthquake hazards remain a critical global challenge. For decades, seismologists have observed that seismic waves of large earthquakes can trigger seismic activity at distances of thousands of kilometers—a phenomenon known as remote (dynamic) triggering. Yet two puzzles persisted: Why do some triggered events occur long after the seismic waves have passed? And why do Rayleigh waves, which carry lower shear stresses than Love waves, appear more effective at triggering?
title: Engineering study reshapes understanding of remotely triggered earthquakes

description: As artificial intelligence makes it easier to pump out convincing reviews for restaurants and travel accommodations, a new study from the University of Massachusetts Amherst suggests a better clue to uncovering suspect reviews isn't the writing—it's the posting habits.
title: On Yelp, actions speak louder than words, study reveals

description: Rivers in the sky bringing moisture to Antarctica during the Southern Hemisphere winter help explain short-term peaks in the world's average temperature, new research has found.
title: How Antarctica helped to set Earth's hottest day on record

description: Researchers at the Institute of Biophysics of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed an AI-assisted method for determining the three-dimensional structures of proteins embedded in membranes. The method, called isSPA-vesicle, was developed by a team led by professor Zhang Xinzheng. The study was published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences on Nov. 16.
title: AI-assisted method advances high-resolution structure classification of membrane proteins in vesicles

description: Some experiments provide only one chance to gather data, but that one shot can be enough for scientists to learn the equations governing a physical system, Cornell researchers have found. They offer a mathematical foundation for learning physical models from fewer experiments.
title: One random shot or none: A mathematical proof for learning a physical system from one experiment

description: NASA's Curiosity Mars rover captured these drifting clouds on Oct. 31, 2026, the 5,061st Martian day, or sol, of the mission. The rover uses its navigation cameras to capture post-sunset clouds, called twilight clouds, which appear for only a short time each fall over Gale Crater, which it has been exploring for more than 14 years.
title: Image: Curiosity spots drifting twilight clouds

description: In an international space experiment led by Adelaide University and conducted in partnership with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), researchers sent experimental medicines more than 300 kilometers (186 miles) above Earth aboard a rocket to investigate whether they could withstand the extreme conditions of space travel.
title: Rocket mission puts a new protective coating for space medicine to the test—and it holds up

description: A research team led by Professor Wang Hui at the Hefei Institutes of Physical Science (HFIPS) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS), in collaboration with Professor Fan Kelong's group at the Institute of Biophysics (IBP) of the CAS, has found that the coordination number of the metal center governs sustained catalysis in single-atom nanozymes through a balance between substrate adsorption and catalytic turnover.
title: Iron single-atom nanozymes enable sustainable catalysis for tumor therapy

description: If you've ever wondered how people manage to pull an "all-nighter" working all-out on an essay or report, new research has found what is going on in our brains when a deadline looms. The new study, published in Nature Communications, was led by professor Matthew Apps from the University of Birmingham's School of Psychology and brought together three studies that included participants having their brains scanned while completing tasks.
title: How looming deadlines may flip the brain's view of hard work

description: Research published today reveals the varied impact of the 2019–2020 Black Summer bushfires on Australia's coastal wetlands, with some ecosystems recovering within a few years while others continue to show signs of significant damage.
title: Black Summer fires left lasting damage to some Australian coastal wetlands

description: A team of researchers at Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg (MLU) and the University of Münster has discovered a new type of atomic oscillation in altermagnets, which exhibit a striking cloverleaf symmetry. The findings were published in the journal Physical Review Letters.
title: Theoretical model describes a new type of atomic oscillation with cloverleaf symmetry in altermagnets

description: Ants live in highly organized colonies, where every insect, from the workers to the queen, knows its place. Typically, queens are larger than workers and have wings. But that is not true of all species. Take moss ants, for example, whose queens can be either winged or wingless. Scientists at Harvard University and the University of Georgia wanted to know what controls the difference.
title: How a single supergene determines whether a moss ant queen is winged or wingless

description: Rain and wind erode fertile soil worldwide. The topsoil, where plants take root and where most of the nutrients are found, is washed away from fields by heavy rain, particularly on slopes and where the ground is not covered by vegetation. Once washed away, it takes a very long time to reform—spanning decades to centuries. To estimate how much soil is lost, researchers use computational models.
title: Soil erosion: US formula used worldwide produces unreliable figures in the Global South

description: Wasps can recognize the faces of their nestmates, much like humans can tell the difference between mom and dad, friend and foe. Now, new research from Wake Forest University shows how the wasp brain makes those distinctions. The finding, said Christopher Jernigan, assistant professor of biology, offers additional perspectives in understanding how animals across species—even humans—process social visual information to distinguish one face from another.
title: Specialized brain cells help wasps recognize other wasp faces

description: Drought is often associated with arid landscapes, but a recent Dalhousie-led study shows it is becoming a growing concern in one of Canada's wetter coastal regions. The research is published in the Journal of Hydrology.
title: Growing drought risk revealed in water‑rich Nova Scotia

description: Astronomers using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) measured the mass of a supermassive black hole in WISE J224607.56−052634.9, also known as W2246-0526. Its light has been stretched by the expansion of the universe to about 5.6 times its original wavelength. This shift, called redshift, tells astronomers that we see the galaxy as it was when the universe was about 1.3 billion years old.
title: ALMA resolves the gravitational reach of a black hole in the early universe

description: You find the product you want on your phone. You compare prices, read reviews and weigh the options. Then, just before tapping "Buy," you hesitate: Maybe I should look at this again on my computer.
title: Why shopping on your phone can make you second-guess a purchase

description: While vast populations face malnourishment and starvation, mountains of food are wasted in affluent countries, which leads to poor food system efficiency, depleted resources, micronutrient losses through ultraprocessed food and environmental degradation.
title: Recycling food waste could return essential minerals to crops, food and animal feed

description: Smoke-affected hops can alter a beer's taste and aroma, but their impact depends on how many are used and when the hops are added during brewing, new research from Oregon State University shows.
title: Smoke-affected hops have greatest impact on beer when added after fermentation, study finds

description: A jaw feature commonly seen by dentists but rarely reported in the human fossil record has been found in an ancient skull, revealing a modern-day medical mystery that dates back at least 2 million years. La Trobe University researchers have identified a pronounced mandibular torus—a harmless bony ridge that forms on the inside of the lower jaw—in a fossil of Australopithecus africanus from Sterkfontein in South Africa.
title: Anatomical variant found in an ancient jaw reveals a modern-day mystery

description: Researchers from the Institute of Applied Ecology (IAE) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and their international collaborators found that prolonged extreme drought favors plant traits associated with acquisition in semiarid grasslands. These changes persist during post-drought recovery. Communities with more acquisitive strategies and greater functional dispersion showed lower sensitivity to drought.
title: Acquisitive plant traits are favored during and following drought

description: If a hidden planet really does exist beyond Neptune, astronomers have identified how it may look and act to explain the mysterious goings-on in the distant reaches of our solar system.
title: Could astronomers be closing in on a hidden planet beyond Neptune?

description: On Friday, Turkish American mathematician and Anthropic employee Levent Alpöge announced he had produced a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most important and famous open problems in mathematics, with the aid of an artificial intelligence (AI) model.
title: 'The sacred object in mathematics': The Riemann hypothesis, AI and a proof no human can read

description: With the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence campaign beginning on Nov. 25, new research suggests public protests can do more than raise awareness of violence against women—they can help reduce sexual violence.
title: Public protests can reduce sexual violence

description: Some active galactic nuclei (AGNs)—galaxies that are powered by actively feeding black holes—undergo rapid changes in their appearance, which manifest as a change in their spectral properties. These are called "changing-look" AGNs. Their appearance changes over time, getting brighter or dimmer, or losing or gaining certain spectral features.
title: Astronomers catch a gas cloud dimming a black hole's glow for weeks

description: When you look out your window, can you see at least three large trees? Is your neighborhood well-shaded by a canopy of trees? And can you walk to a park or other high-quality green space in less than five minutes? These three questions lie at the heart of the 3-30-300 rule, a benchmark that's increasingly used to evaluate urban greenness.
title: New study uses 3-30-300 rule to evaluate urban greenness in five major Canadian cities, finds room for improvement

description: Despite all the hype about a new space economy, humanity has yet to reap much benefit from off-world mining, manufacturing or space tourism.
title: Space entrepreneurs should look to 16th-century spice trade for inspiration

description: Do you dream of going viral? New research by SFI program postdoctoral fellow Shuhao Fu and linguists at Zhejiang University could offer the insights you need.
title: TED talks and podcasts with slower shifts between ideas tend to be more popular

description: How will we eat in 2050? Will AI-generated, personalized nutrition programs suggest we eat edible insects and drink a glass of synthetic milk for dinner?
title: How is Gen Z changing what we eat? These writers found out by asking over 20,000 young people

description: The value of a stone tool can long outlast its first sharp edge. Across 27 locations in southwest China, archaeologists have found evidence of a toolmaking approach that preserved enough stone to allow repeated sharpening—and sometimes the same piece was used as both a tool and a source of fresh flakes for new cutting edges.
title: Reduce, resharpen, reuse: Ancient stone tools reveal a regional pattern in southwest China

description: Have you ever wondered why restaurants include outrageously expensive bottles of wine on their menus?
title: A trick marketers use to sell you things can also persuade rats to enter traps

description: Researchers from Curtin University's Timescales of Mineral Systems Group at the Curtin Frontier Institute for Geoscience Solutions (CFIGS) have developed a suite of analytical tools to improve understanding of Australia's heavy mineral deposits, paving the way for more efficient mineral sands exploration.
title: New toolkit enhances mineral sands understanding

description: In the whirlwind of work demands and family obligations—including planning vacations and holiday celebrations—many parents assume they need to go all out and spend lots of money to build family bonds.
title: How to use small, everyday moments to strengthen family connections

description: Beneath a tangle of highways in the Malaysian capital Kuala Lumpur, a family of otters rolls around in a patch of riverside sand, delighting the few passersby who notice them.
title: Kuala Lumpur otters raise river revival hopes

description: Britain has long had a reputation for rain. But as it adapts to a warmer, drier climate, the U.K. is racing to complete a huge new reservoir, its first in over three decades.
title: UK digging new reservoirs to fight persistent droughts

description: In a new paper published in the American Journal of Botany, a team of scientists from the U.S. and UK reveal an incredible fossil from the mid-Cretaceous period (around 100 million years ago), opening up a new window into the early evolutionary history of modern-day plants.
title: Hidden for 100 million years: X-rays reveal an ancient flower from the age of dinosaurs

description: Fifty-two million years ago, the Pacific tectonic plate began to slide under the Philippine Sea plate, forming the Mariana Trench, the deepest known valley on the Earth's ocean floor. The deepest part of this abyss, the Challenger Deep, is almost 11,000 meters (36,000 feet) below sea level. But why is it so deep? Scientists trying to answer this question sent a remotely operated vehicle to collect samples around the Deep, where they found evidence of the world's deepest underwater explosive volcanic eruptions.
title: Robot submarine exploring world's deepest ocean trench finds unprecedented volcanic activity
